# What fixes the P14 coupling?

At fixed q = 0.000865 and z_t = 10, a smaller early coupling β requires a faster field, k = |q|/β. The extra field energy can offset the slower atomic expansion during nucleosynthesis. The same field is still present at recombination, where its effect on the CMB peaks offers an independent test.

At β = 0.00257634, H_atomic/H_std at 0.1 MeV is 1.00016, yet the scalar carries 3.55% of the energy at z = 1089.95. At β = 1 these values are 0.98581 and 0.0219%.

## Which couplings pass the smooth-fraction comparison?

Gómez-Valent et al. give approximate two-sigma upper limits for a smooth component around decoupling. The limit depends on the data combination. Each row applies one published limit to the P14 background and evaluates the abundance likelihood from that crossing to the top of the scan. These are translations of related models. P14 has no fitted CMB confidence interval here. [Gómez-Valent et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.11065)

| Upper Ωφ at recombination | β passing within scan | L(standard)/L(P14), helium + deuterium |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.6% | 0.00637–1 | 6.5–15.5 |
| 0.4% | 0.00787–1 | 8.6–15.5 |

Both comparisons put cancellation below the indicated β range. At β = 0.01 and 0.02, standard expansion fits the abundances 10.7 and 14.1 times better. Choosing β to remove the deuterium discrepancy would use up deuterium as an independent test. The project rule requires the mechanism to be fixed before seeing the discrepancy. These likelihood ratios do not score P14.

Da Fonseca et al. find k < 0.056 at 68% for a constant field velocity. At fixed q this would imply β > 0.0154. Their coupling acts only on cold dark matter and persists today. [da Fonseca et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.14889)

Goh et al. find a pre-recombination coupling below 0.026 at 68% in their binned cold-dark-matter model. Growth and lensing can therefore probe larger couplings. Transferring that upper bound to P14 would require its baryon coupling and switch-off in the perturbation equations. [Goh et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.13588)

SPT, Planck and ACT give N_eff = 2.96 (+0.21, −0.24) with helium free. At cancellation the field adds the energy equivalent of ΔN_eff = 0.216 after pair annihilation. Matching the approximate upper two-sigma endpoint by energy alone gives β ≳ 0.0021, which admits cancellation. A smooth scalar and free-streaming neutrinos drive different perturbations, so energy matching alone gives no P14 likelihood. [SPT-3G D1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20707)

## Expansion and field energy

The background uses the conserving scalar history at fixed atomic temperature. At recombination, Ωφ = U/(B+U) includes matter and radiation in B. In pure radiation domination Ωφ = k²/4. ΔN_eff divides the field energy on this attractor by the energy of one neutrino species after pair annihilation, with standard N_eff = 3.044. Today the kinetic energy gives wφ = −1 + k²/(3Ωφ₀).

## Abundances and late expansion

Each yield ratio divides a network run by its standard-expansion run at ω_b = 0.02237. We apply those ratios to the published Planck Gaussian-process deuterium and PRIMAT helium predictions. The signed distances from LBT helium and PDG deuterium use the same errors and shared baryon-density covariance as the P14 abundance analysis. Negative distances mean the predicted abundance is low. [Abundance inputs](p14_bbn_status.md) · [Network and validation](p14_physical_model.md)

For DESI DR2 BAO alone we use E²(z) = C_m(1+z)³ + (1−C_m)(1+z)^(k²), neglecting late radiation. We profile C_m and H₀r_d independently at each β, retaining the within-bin distance covariances. The reference fit at k = 0 gives χ² = 10.54. At cancellation it is 9.71. BAO alone admits cancellation. [DESI DR2 measurements](../data/desi_dr2_bao.csv)

**The missing calculation** is a CLASS/Cobaya fit of the coupled scalar, baryon and cold-dark-matter perturbations to Planck/ACT spectra and lensing plus DESI. Profile β with free ω_b and helium, reconstruct the potential at each trial cosmology, and compute recombination in atomic units. This would test cancellation independently of deuterium and supply the baryon density for its abundance test.
